courses.title: Python Programming
courses.schedule: Self-paced with live mentor Q&A every Tuesday at 4:00 PM
courses.prerequisites: None! Basic computer literacy is sufficient. Perfect for first-time programmers.
courses.description: Master Python programming fundamentals, data structures, algorithms, and object-oriented development with hands-on exercises and real-world projects.
learningOutcomes: Write clean, idiomatic Python code for scripts and automation
Understand control flow, conditionals, and looping mechanisms
Master core data structures (Lists, Dictionaries, Sets, Tuples)
Build modular programs using functions and classes (OOP)
Handle errors, file I/O operations, and standard Python libraries
Develop a fully functional capstone automation project

syllabus.title: Introduction to Python & Setup
syllabus.summary: Environment installation, IDE setup, interactive shell, first Hello World program.

syllabus.title: Variables, Data Types & Operators
syllabus.summary: Numeric types, strings, boolean logic, input/output formatting, type casting.

syllabus.title: Control Flow & Loops
syllabus.summary: If/elif/else statements, for loops, while loops, break and continue statements.

syllabus.title: Functions & Scope
syllabus.summary: Function definition, parameters, return values, lambda functions, global vs local scope.

syllabus.title: Data Structures in Depth
syllabus.summary: Lists manipulation, slicing, tuples, dictionary mapping, sets, and comprehension.

syllabus.title: Object-Oriented Programming (OOP)
syllabus.summary: Classes, objects, constructors (__init__), inheritance, encapsulation, polymorphism.

syllabus.title: File Handling & Exception Management
syllabus.summary: Reading/writing text and CSV files, try/except/finally blocks, custom exceptions.

syllabus.title: Capstone Project & Final Assessment
syllabus.summary: Building a CLI student grade analyzer and portfolio project.

faq.question: Can I learn Python with no prior programming experience?
faq.answer: Absolutely! Python Programming is designed specifically for beginners, starting with the absolute basics.

faq.question: When can I claim my certificate?
faq.answer: Once you complete all 8 modules and submit the capstone assignment, your certificate is automatically unlocked.

courses.title: Full Stack Web Development

instructor.name: Prof. Priya Sharma
instructor.title: Lead Full Stack Architect & Frontend Specialist

courses.schedule: Self-paced with live coding labs every Thursday at 5:00 PM
courses.prerequisites: Basic understanding of computers and web browsers. No prior programming needed.
courses.description: Complete web development path covering HTML5, CSS3, modern JavaScript, frontend frameworks, backend APIs, and databases.
learningOutcomes: Craft responsive layouts using CSS Flexbox, Grid, and mobile-first principles
Master modern JavaScript ES6+, DOM manipulation, and asynchronous APIs
Build modular client-side apps using modern component architectures
Create RESTful APIs and microservices with Node.js and Express
Connect relational and document databases with backend services
Deploy production-ready full-stack applications with CI/CD

syllabus.title: HTML5 Semantics & Accessible Structure
syllabus.summary: Semantic elements, forms, audio/video integration, SEO meta tags.

syllabus.title: Modern CSS3, Flexbox & CSS Grid
syllabus.summary: Box model, responsive units, Flexbox layouts, Grid alignment, animations.

syllabus.title: Responsive Design & Mobile-First Workflow
syllabus.summary: Media queries, responsive typography, fluid images, adaptive UI components.

syllabus.title: JavaScript Essentials & DOM Manipulation
syllabus.summary: Variables, functions, events, query selectors, dynamic DOM modification.

syllabus.title: Modern ES6+ & Asynchronous JavaScript
syllabus.summary: Arrow functions, destructuring, promises, async/await, Fetch API.

syllabus.title: Frontend Frameworks & UI Architecture
syllabus.summary: Component lifecycle, state management, props, reactive user interfaces.

syllabus.title: Backend Fundamentals with Node.js & Express
syllabus.summary: Node runtime, HTTP servers, Express routes, middleware, request handling.

syllabus.title: RESTful API Design & JSON Services
syllabus.summary: Endpoints, CRUD methods, status codes, query parameters, data validation.

syllabus.title: Database Integration & Authentication
syllabus.summary: Connecting databases, password hashing, JWT tokens, session security.

syllabus.title: Full Stack Capstone Project & Deployment
syllabus.summary: End-to-end full stack web app deployed on cloud hosting.

faq.question: What frontend framework is taught in this course?
faq.answer: The course covers modern vanilla JavaScript ES6+ deeply followed by component fundamentals in modern frameworks.

faq.question: Is full stack web development suitable for beginners?
faq.answer: Yes! The first 5 modules build a solid foundation in HTML, CSS, and JavaScript before progressing to backend.

courses.title: Database Management Systems
courses.schedule: Self-paced with weekly interactive SQL query labs on Wednesdays at 3:30 PM
courses.prerequisites: Basic understanding of programming logic and elementary computer science concepts.
courses.description: Comprehensive coverage of database architectures, relational schema design, SQL querying, normalization (1NF-BCNF), transactions, ACID properties, and indexing.
learningOutcomes: Design relational database schemas with ER modeling and constraints
Write complex SQL queries with joins, grouping, and aggregate functions
Normalize database tables from 1NF to BCNF to remove redundancy
Optimize queries with B-Tree indexes and execution plan analysis
Manage concurrent transactions with ACID compliance and locking protocols
Understand NoSQL key-value and document data models (MongoDB)

syllabus.title: Introduction to DBMS & Relational Model
syllabus.summary: Database concepts, relational algebra, primary/foreign keys, schema integrity.

syllabus.title: Entity-Relationship (ER) Modeling
syllabus.summary: Entities, attributes, cardinality, ER diagrams, mapping ER models to tables.

syllabus.title: SQL Fundamentals (DDL, DML, DCL)
syllabus.summary: CREATE, ALTER, DROP, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, and GRANT permissions.

syllabus.title: Advanced SQL Queries & Joins
syllabus.summary: INNER JOIN, LEFT/RIGHT JOIN, GROUP BY, HAVING, subqueries, view definitions.

syllabus.title: Database Normalization (1NF to BCNF)
syllabus.summary: Functional dependencies, 1NF, 2NF, 3NF, BCNF decomposition without data loss.

syllabus.title: Indexing & Query Optimization
syllabus.summary: Clustered/non-clustered indexes, B+ Trees, hashing, execution plan profiling.

syllabus.title: Transactions & ACID Properties
syllabus.summary: Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability, commit/rollback states.

syllabus.title: Concurrency Control & Recovery
syllabus.summary: Two-phase locking (2PL), deadlock prevention, write-ahead logging (WAL).

syllabus.title: NoSQL Databases & Modern Data Stores
syllabus.summary: Document stores (MongoDB), JSON queries, key-value stores, distributed databases.

faq.question: What database software will we use?
faq.answer: We use MySQL and PostgreSQL for relational databases, plus MongoDB for NoSQL concepts.

faq.question: What is normalization and why does it matter?
faq.answer: Normalization is the process of structuring a database to reduce data redundancy and improve data integrity.

courses.title: Introduction to Artificial Intelligence

instructor.name: Dr. Meena Krishnan
instructor.title: AI Research Director & Former Principal Data Scientist

certificate.type: Professional Certificate in Artificial Intelligence Foundations

courses.schedule: Course Completed - Full permanent access to lecture notes, labs, and replays
courses.prerequisites: High-school mathematics (basic linear algebra and probability) and introductory Python programming.
courses.description: Explore the foundations of artificial intelligence, search algorithms, heuristic reasoning, machine learning basics, computer vision, NLP, and ethical AI governance.
learningOutcomes: Formulate intelligent agent problems in observable and stochastic environments
Implement uninformed and heuristic search algorithms (BFS, DFS, A*, Minimax)
Understand knowledge representation and propositional/first-order logic
Train fundamental machine learning algorithms for classification and regression
Explore foundational neural network architectures and deep learning concepts
Analyze ethical implications, fairness, transparency, and safety in AI systems

syllabus.title: Overview of AI, Agents & Environments
syllabus.summary: Turing test, history of AI, agent types, environmental properties.

syllabus.title: Problem Solving with Search Algorithms
syllabus.summary: State space search, BFS, DFS, A* heuristic search, adversarial search.

syllabus.title: Knowledge Representation & Logic
syllabus.summary: Propositional logic, inference rules, First-Order Logic (FOL), ontologies.

syllabus.title: Introduction to Machine Learning
syllabus.summary: Supervised learning, linear regression, decision trees, neural network basics.

syllabus.title: NLP & Computer Vision Fundamentals
syllabus.summary: Tokenization, bag-of-words, image convolutions, pretrained vision models.

syllabus.title: AI Ethics, Bias Mitigation & Capstone
syllabus.summary: Algorithmic bias, explainability, safety guidelines, final AI project.

faq.question: Can I download my certificate for this course?
faq.answer: Yes! Your certificate (ID: EDU-AI-2026-884) is issued and can be viewed or downloaded from your profile or certificates page.

faq.question: Can I still review completed materials?
faq.answer: Yes, you have lifetime archived access to all completed lessons, quizzes, and resources.
